product: What Robinhood actually sells today is a multi-line US retail financial platform, not just a trading app: commission-free equities, options, crypto, futures and event (prediction) contracts, margin lending, Gold subscriptions, retirement accounts, advisory via TradePMR, banking, a credit card, and listed private-markets funds. In Q2 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30, reported 2026-07-29) total net revenues were a record $1.31B, up 32% YoY, split into transaction-based revenue of $776M (+44%) - event contracts $156M (up over 10x), options $342M (+29%), equities $129M (+95%), crypto $100M (-38%) - net interest revenue of $389M (+9%) and other revenue of $143M (+54%, Trump Account service fees, Gold subscriptions, card). Net income rose 48% to $573M (diluted EPS $0.62, including $0.14 of RVI deconsolidation gains) on $741M adjusted EBITDA, and management said 13 business lines - Robinhood Legend and the credit card newly among them - have now crossed $100M annualized.
demand: Q3 - demand is moving with VOLUME and MIX, not price: they are selling more, and a different thing. Q2 2026 records were equity notional $956B (+85% YoY), options 774M contracts (+50%), event contracts 13.6B (over 10x), net deposits $21.7B (LTM $75.7B, 27% of assets), total platform assets $369B (+32%), funded customers 28.4M (+7%), ARPU $187 (+24%) and a margin book of $21.6B (+127%); the freshest company data, the 2026-09-10 August 2026 operating release, shows the mix shifting further to prediction markets and margin but also sequential deceleration - equity notional $335.4B (+1% MoM, +68% YoY), options 292.5M contracts (-10% MoM, +50% YoY), event contracts 4.7B (-23% MoM, +15x YoY), crypto notional $17.5B (-38% YoY with the Robinhood app itself -46%), net deposits $4.0B in August (a 14% annualized growth rate versus 28% in Q2) and LTM net deposits $74.1B (24% growth). Q5 - customers are retail and unconcentrated with no single-customer concentration: 28.6M funded customers at end-August 2026 (+1.90M YoY), Gold subscribers 4.8M (+39% YoY, 17% adoption, roughly 40% of new funded customers take Gold) and net deposits running at 24-28% of assets imply low churn, but revenue mix is concentrating in prediction-market and margin-active cohorts while cash sweep balances fell 9% YoY to $31.2B and securities lending revenue fell 32% YoY to $36M in August.
pricing_power: Pricing power is weak on core trading and rate-driven rather than priced elsewhere. Robinhood is commission-free, so transaction revenue comes from payment-for-order-flow and market-maker rebates and take rates - raising ticket prices would destroy the volume that drives the model - and net interest revenue ($389M in Q2, the largest single line) is a function of rates and balances, not pricing. The genuine if narrow pricing power sits in bundling (Gold at $5/month, 4.8M subscribers, roughly 40% of new funded customers sign up), in take rates on new categories (event contracts, margin lending, advisory) and in card interchange on the Gold Card's $17B annualized purchase volume. Net: growth is being bought with product breadth and subscription attach rather than with price, while lower short-term rates and a 9%-YoY cash-sweep decline are actively working against the largest revenue line.
competition: Q4 - key infrastructure suppliers are concentrated and just changed: Robinhood internalized event-contract execution with Rothera in June 2026 (a CFTC-licensed exchange and clearinghouse run through a joint venture with Susquehanna International Group, over 3.5B contracts traded), then on 2026-09-08 designated OG.com - Crypto.com's spin-off operating the CFTC-regulated NADEX venue, independently valued at $5B inside Citadel Securities' $20B Crypto.com round - as its prediction-markets infrastructure and clearing provider, taking equity stakes in both Crypto.com and OG.com and beginning a phased US rollout that day. Other supplier-type dependencies are exchange and market-maker venues and rebates for equities and options, acquired Bitstamp for crypto execution and liquidity, Arbitrum/Offchain Labs for Robinhood Chain, and card and stablecoin rails; the change worth flagging is that the fastest-growing revenue line now runs through one external venue. Q6 - if Robinhood is right, the specific losers are Kalshi and Polymarket and the incumbent sportsbooks (DraftKings, Flutter/FanDuel) in prediction markets - note the American Gaming Association forecasts a FLAT 2026 legal sports-betting handle while prediction-market growth concentrates in Kalshi/Polymarket/HOOD - plus Coinbase, Kraken and Webull in crypto, Schwab, Morgan Stanley/E*TRADE, Interactive Brokers and SoFi in active-trader retail brokerage, and incumbent advisories, transfer agents and custodians displaced by TradePMR, tokenized stock tokens and the listed RVI/RVII funds.
team: Chairman and CEO Vlad Tenev; CFO Shiv Verma, who continues as principal financial officer after ceasing to serve as principal accounting officer on 2026-06-25; Dara Bazzano was appointed principal accounting officer effective 2026-06-25 (Chief Accounting Officer since April 2026, previously Cross Country Consulting, T-Mobile US, CBRE and Gap, and an assurance partner at PwC and KPMG). Other named leaders include Steve Quirk (Chief Brokerage Officer), Steph Guild (Chief Investment Officer), JB Mackenzie (VP/GM, Futures and Prediction Markets) and Sarah Pinto (President, Robinhood Ventures Fund I). The notable 2026 personnel event remains the 2026-06-16 Form 8-K reduction in force of approximately 10% of full-time employees (~$20M severance and benefits plus ~$8M of share-based compensation accrued in Q2 2026), explicitly taken from a position of business strength, alongside a separate Form 8-K item 5.02 officer change filed 2026-05-08 whose specifics were not retrieved this run.
market_strategy: Q1 - what changed in the last 90 days that a reasonable investor would not have known a year ago: Q2 2026 made prediction markets a material, disclosed revenue line ($156M in one quarter, up over 10x; 13.6B contracts), a 10% workforce reduction was executed from strength, a $2.2B June 2026 convertible notes offering closed (with $290M of concurrent share repurchases and cash rising to $5.4B), Trump Accounts launched 2026-07-04 (7M+ sign-ups), Robinhood Chain mainnet and stock tokens in 120+ countries went live, WonderFi closed for the Canada entry, Singapore received its MAS capital markets services licence on 2026-07-01, and on 2026-09-08 the prediction-market supply chain shifted to OG.com with equity stakes in Crypto.com and OG.com. Q2 - what is true today that was not knowable yesterday: nothing company-specific dated to 2026-09-24/25 was found; the freshest dated items are the 2026-09-23 IR '5 Years Since IPO' supplemental presentation, the 2026-09-23 Barclays maintain at $105, the 2026-09-21 Bernstein maintain at $160 and the 2026-09-10 August operating-data release, with the live catalyst still the CLARITY Act process in the Senate. Q7 - the strongest evidence CONTRADICTING the bull case is inside the company's own newest disclosure: in the 2026-09-10 August operating release event-contract volume fell 23% MoM (to 4.7B from 6.1B) and options contracts fell 10% MoM, net deposits slowed to $4.0B (14% annualized) from $21.7B in Q2, crypto notional fell 38% YoY, cash sweep fell 9% YoY and net interest revenue grew only 9% despite 26-32% asset growth - the fastest-growing line decelerated sequentially and depends on one external venue, even as the stock re-rated (21-day momentum +29.7% on 75.1% 63-day volatility and a forward P/E near 47 on consensus FY2026 EPS of $2.54). Q8 - if management's stated strategy plays out, revenue compounds on 24-27% net deposit growth with operating leverage and EPS momentum (consensus FY2026 revenue about $5.2B, +16%), but with the re-rating largely already done the 12-month payoff is continued compounding rather than further multiple expansion, and the $57-$170 target dispersion plus the target-level anti-signal argue against counting on re-rating. Q9 - the specific way management is wrong is extrapolating a policy-fragile, event-driven prediction-market boom as durable while crypto shrinks (-38% YoY) and net interest revenue decelerates on rate cuts; a CFTC rulemaking or state-gaming injunction against event contracts, or a post-football-season volume air-pocket of the kind August already hinted at (-23% MoM), would hit the fastest-growing line hard and expose that 13 '$100M+ business lines' is breadth without a defensible moat. Q10 - second- and third-order beneficiaries if the trend continues are Crypto.com and OG.com and Citadel Securities (which set the $20B and $5B valuations), Susquehanna International Group (Rothera JV), Arbitrum/Offchain Labs (Robinhood Chain settles to Ethereum via Arbitrum, 200M+ testnet transactions disclosed 2026-09-02), CFTC-regulated infrastructure vendors such as Trading Technologies, card networks and interchange rails behind the Gold Card's $17B annualized volume, crypto custody and stablecoin rails, the TradePMR RIA network, and HOOD's own index and ETF complex including leveraged HOOD ETFs and the listed RVI/RVII funds. Stated strategy for the next 12 months - make everyone an owner via product velocity: scale prediction markets on OG.com infrastructure, push Robinhood Chain and stock tokens globally (120+ countries), grow Trump Accounts, Gold and Platinum cards, banking and retirement, expand advisory (TradePMR) and international (Canada, Singapore, EU perpetuals, UK crypto), and ship Agentic Trading, while management tightened its 2026 Adjusted Operating Expenses and SBC outlook to $2.675-2.775B in the Q2 2026 release.
bull: This program's own standing finding names HOOD as the one listed name on the WINNING side of the AGA 'flat handle' leak: event-contract revenue ($156M Q2) already exceeds crypto revenue, equity notional +85% y/y, options contracts +50%, event contracts up >10x, funded customers +7%, ARPU +24%. Robinhood internalized execution via Rothera (a CFTC-licensed exchange/clearinghouse JV with Susquehanna, launched June 2026, >3.5B contracts traded) -- vertical integration that DKNG/FLUT do not have. Q3 is confirmed for 2026-11-04.
bear: The same 2026-09-13 court ruling that hurts DKNG's competitors (prediction markets ARE gambling, not federally regulated trading) is a structural risk to Robinhood's own CFTC-based event-contract model -- if it extends, HOOD could be pulled into the state-by-state gambling licensing regime it has so far avoided. The CLARITY Act cloture vote (09-15) is a binary legislative catalyst on the crypto/token side that cuts either way and is outside company control.
falsifier: A state or federal action forcing Robinhood's event contracts under state gambling licensing (raising costs / restricting states) would falsify the bull thesis; continued event-contract revenue growth through the Nov 4 print without new licensing friction would confirm it.
